client_alerts.headline: Microsoft 365 Copilot agents can now write to connected systems
client_alerts.body: Connector **write actions** are generally available in Copilot Chat and Cowork. Depending on the connector, Copilot can create, update or **delete** records in connected apps. Clients should treat these agents as privileged change actors: review connector scopes, log agent actions, and confirm that DR backups can roll back agent-made changes.

client_alerts.headline: Claude Meetings joins client calls as a visible participant
client_alerts.body: Claude can now join Google Meet calls (beta, Team/Enterprise) to take notes and draft docs. Before using it on client calls, confirm that recording and AI-processing disclosure is covered by the engagement terms.

top_moves.title: Outage week turns into a BCP refresh mandate
top_moves.body: After **six major outages in six days** (Microsoft 365 on Nov 12, the FAA ground stop on Nov 13, Apple iCloud on Nov 17), Gartner told CIOs to urgently refresh scenario plans, BIAs and DR. Forrester and Fortune say boards are now asking whether this could happen to them, which is a direct opening for resilience advisory work.

top_moves.title: Copilot agents get write access to line-of-business data
top_moves.body: Microsoft made connector write actions generally available as the post-Ignite rollouts land, with the Autopilot always-on agent queued for Frontier customers. Agents that can delete data belong in change-management and recovery scope.

top_moves.title: Anthropic stock cools after record IPO
top_moves.body: After opening at $111.50 against an $83 offer price, ANTH gave back much of its first-day pop, and Goldman's research flags heavy cash burn ahead. Anthropic now publishes quarterly results, which gives clients a new input for vendor-risk reviews of a key AI supplier.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol reportedly shipped Nov 18, aimed at professional work at lower compute cost.
providers.detail: A Nov 18 digest reports that GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol were released for professional work at lower compute cost. Not yet confirmed on OpenAI's own release notes. Images 2.6 (Nov 4) is the latest confirmed ChatGPT release, and a beta business hub lets organizations verify their presence in ChatGPT.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Post-IPO trading cools, with deprecations landing in 7 days.
providers.detail: ANTH priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and has drifted down since. Recent product changes: Desktop release channels (Nov 17), Claude Meetings beta and self-hosted Managed Agents (Nov 12), Fable 5.2 at lower prices (Nov 9). Sonnet 4.5 retirement and Opus 4.8 fast-mode removal happen **Nov 30**.
providers.alertReason: Claude Meetings joins client calls; check consent and disclosure

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: No new Gemini release in the last 48 hours.
providers.detail: The Gemini 4 line (Carbon Nov 10, Hydrogen Nov 12, Neon last week) is still being absorbed. Nothing new over the weekend.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Still no Grok 5; Grok 4.7 and Voice 3.0 remain the latest releases.
providers.detail: No release since Grok Voice 3.0 (Oct 14). grok-imagine-image-quality was retired Nov 2. The company now operates as SpaceXAI.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Muse Ember (Nov 9) is the latest release; the Muse Spark 1.2 weights are still unshipped.
providers.detail: No new Llama; Llama 4 remains the last Llama release. Meta's open-weight pivot to Apache-licensed Muse Glimmer stands, and the promised Muse Spark 1.2 weights have not appeared.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release since Large 4 and the Studio agent workflows.
providers.detail: Large 4 with Studio event triggers and visual workflow graphs is still current. Mistral remains the EU-sovereign option for clients with data-residency constraints.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Teammates agents (Nov 5, Max only) are still the latest release; the Amazon cease-and-desist is unresolved.
providers.detail: Teammates, local Computer on Mac and Voice mode all date to Nov 6. Amazon's cease-and-desist over Comet completing purchases is still unresolved, a reminder that agentic browsing carries terms-of-service risk.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Post-Ignite November rollouts land, including GA of connector write actions.
providers.detail: Unified Chat/Cowork history, Projects in Copilot Chat, and OneNote and Planner Cowork plugins are rolling out worldwide. Connector write actions are GA. Autopilot (an always-on cloud agent) is listed for Frontier, but Message Center says timing will follow. A Nov 12 M365 outage lasted roughly a day.
providers.alertReason: Agents can create, update or delete data in connected apps

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No confirmed update in the last 48 hours.
providers.detail: Usage-based billing (since June) and Claude Haiku 5.5 support (Oct 5) are the latest notable changes.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new update; Claude supply continues after the OpenAI model cutoff.
providers.detail: Following SpaceXAI's acquisition, OpenAI model supply was set to end around Nov 12 (extended per earlier reports). Anthropic says it will keep supplying Claude.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release in the last 48 hours; Gamma 5 is still current.
providers.detail: Gamma 5 (Oct 6) brought a redesigned editor, a stronger agent and Slack/Notion context sources.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; the Oct 19 agents, BYOK and credit-system update is the latest.
providers.detail: Notion 3.8 (Oct 13) and the Oct 19 AI update (more capable agents, a cheaper Auto model, bring-your-own-key, improved MCP, new credit system) are still current.

month_themes.then: AI-discovered vulnerabilities driving a patch scramble; agentic AI in supply-chain attacks; banks containing third-party AI agents
month_themes.now: Operational resilience after a week of outages; AI agents with write access to business data; AI vendors maturing into public companies

Offer a fixed-scope **post-outage resilience review** citing the Gartner Nov 17 guidance; move any Sonnet 4.5 API workflows before Nov 30.
Build a one-slide 'Could this happen to us?' board answer using the Nov 12–17 outage timeline.

community.signal: The Qwen 'open source to the end' pledge drew ~4.5K score (Nov 2 digest; no fresh weekly data found).
community.so_what: Open-weight Chinese models are still the main local alternative as Meta retreats from open weights; check provenance and policy before client use.

community.signal: The Altman local-inference comment thread hit ~6.5K score and ~2.8K comments, spilling into subscription-cancellation posts on r/ChatGPT.
community.so_what: User trust in hosted-AI terms is fragile; a local or offline fallback is a legitimate continuity control.

community.signal: A reported Qwen 4 leak (qwen4-max, coder-plus, omni-120b) scored 739; Qwen teasers followed on Nov 6.
community.so_what: A major open-weight release may be imminent; watch before recommending a local model stack.

watch.title: Nov 30: Claude Sonnet 4.5 retires, Opus 4.8 fast mode removed
watch.body: Seven days left. Move any pinned API calls or automations to current models and re-test their outputs.

watch.title: Copilot Autopilot and agent write actions
watch.body: The Autopilot always-on agent is queued for Frontier tenants with timing TBD. Watch the Message Center and lock down connector permissions before it arrives.

watch.title: Post-outage board questions
watch.body: Gartner, Forrester and Fortune all framed the Nov 12–17 outages as a resilience wake-up call. Expect client RFPs for BIA and DR refreshes over the next two weeks.

watch.title: Perplexity vs Amazon over agentic purchasing
watch.body: The cease-and-desist over Comet buying on Amazon could set a precedent for whether agents may act on third-party sites; this matters for clients' agent policies.

watch.title: Qwen 4 open-weight release
watch.body: Leaks and teasers point to an imminent launch. Assess it for local or offline continuity use cases, with provenance review.
